note: Hand-curated roster of active Chicago bikeway/trail proposals and projects. Selection criteria: an official record exists, the outcome is unresolved, and the set keeps geographic spread — under-covered South and West Side projects are deliberately included; news-coverage volume is not a criterion. Each status is a volunteer-reviewed judgment backed by the citations listed with it (status_as_of = when it was last reviewed); the linked official page is always authoritative. Attached coverage is verbatim headlines from the news_items dataset, matched by each project's curated phrases (auditable via `via`); an empty coverage list measures press attention, not project activity.

projects.name: Bloomingdale Trail (606) Extension
projects.status_note: Funded in part: a federal earmark secured by Rep. Quigley (~$1.4M reported toward Phase II) against an estimated $30–40M total, with state/local sources still being assembled. Preliminary engineering wrapping up; construction expected to start around late 2026, completion late 2027 (timeline per Block Club, Jan 2025).
projects.description: Extend the elevated 606/Bloomingdale Trail east from its current end at Ashland Avenue, under the Kennedy Expressway, to Elston Avenue, coordinated with the Lincoln Yards site.

citations.title: The 606's Bloomingdale Trail Extension Delayed, With Completion Now Expected By Late 2027

projects.name: Archer Avenue Traffic Safety Project
projects.status_note: Protected bike lanes with concrete curbs, pedestrian refuge islands, and curb extensions were installed in Brighton Park; after sustained resident protests, the city restored 17 parking spaces across three sub-segments in April 2026 while keeping the concrete-protected lanes — CDOT says there are no plans to remove the project's core safety features.
projects.description: Complete Streets safety redesign of Archer Avenue in Brighton Park (12th Ward), on a corridor CDOT tied to a majority of the area's serious pedestrian/cyclist injuries.

projects.name: Grand Avenue Protected Bike Lanes (Phase 2)
projects.status_note: Phase 1 (36th Ward stretch) was built in 2023; Phase 2 toward Ogden slipped to a 2026 start and is now being built amid weekly protests and counter-rallies. CDOT and Ald. La Spata (1st) cite fewer severe crashes and less speeding on the completed segments.
projects.description: Multi-phase Complete Streets project adding protected bike lanes along Grand Avenue through West Town (1st/27th/36th wards).

projects.name: DuSable Lake Shore Drive Redesign (Redefine the Drive)
projects.status_note: Joint CDOT/IDOT/CMAP reconstruction study; as of a May 2026 CMAP meeting the alternatives analysis was still being revised with no preferred alternative finalized. Proposed bike/ped pieces include a separated overpass at Addison and an expanded shared-use underpass at Hawthorne; advocates are pressing against a car-centric 8-lane option.
projects.description: Reconstruction of the North DuSable Lake Shore Drive corridor, including its bike and pedestrian crossings and the Lakefront Trail interface.

projects.name: Englewood Nature Trail
projects.status_note: $20M in grants secured against an $80M estimate. The site is in a clearing and viaduct-repair phase; construction has been pushed to 2027 with completion expected in 2029 (timeline per Chicago YIMBY/Hoodline, May 2026).
projects.description: Rails-to-trails conversion of a former Norfolk Southern elevated line: 1.8 miles from Damen to Halsted in Englewood, led by Grow Greater Englewood with the city.

citations.title: Updated Timeline Revealed For Englewood Nature Trail

projects.name: Weber Spur Trail
projects.status_note: Secured $850,000 in federal funding (Rep. Quigley community project, Feb 2026) against a ~$70M estimate; land acquisition from Union Pacific remains unresolved after roughly two decades. Construction target is 2029.
projects.description: 1.7-mile trail on a former Union Pacific right-of-way through LaBagh Woods on the Northwest Side, connecting toward the North Branch Trail.

citations.title: Weber Spur Bike Trail Secures Federal Funding
